action: UK banks, insurers and other in-scope firms: read GC26/9 / CP17/26 and send responses to the FCA and Bank of England by 26 February 2027.
exec: UK regulators are drafting guidance on board accountability and recovery from cyber attacks for banks, insurers and similar firms. It is not final.
org: FCA, PRA and Bank of England
plain: UK financial regulators have opened a consultation on draft cyber guidance. It says boards and a named senior manager are accountable for cyber risk, and firms need a tested plan to recover from attacks.

summary: The FCA, PRA and Bank of England opened a joint consultation on 19 November 2026 (FCA GC26/9, PRA CP17/26) on cyber risk and resilience management. The FCA says firms should make the board and senior managers accountable for cyber risk, with a named senior manager, and have a tested plan to recover from attacks. The Bank of England says it proposes no new rules. Responses close 26 February 2027.
title: UK regulators consult on cyber risk and resilience guidance for financial firms
